title: NBA disburses around Rs. 3.79 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing mechanism to 33 States/UTs and National Institutes
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 AUG 2026 10:46AM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) disbursed ₹3.79 crore under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism to 33 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), UT Biodiversity Councils, and ICAR-NBPGR, bringing total cumulative ABS releases past ₹166 crore.
ABS funds are collected under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 from commercial companies accessing biological and genetic resources (such as vegetable seeds and livestock germplasm).

Disbursement to states is proportioned using cultivation-area data from the Ministry of Agriculture, with funds earmarked for People's Biodiversity Registers (PBRs), in-situ/ex-situ conservation, and Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs).
The ABS framework directly supports the Nagoya Protocol and Targets 4 and 13 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework regarding fair and equitable benefit sharing and genetic diversity.

date:

upsc_summary: The 259th Standing Committee Report on Cyber Crime highlights gaps in IT Rules 2021, recommending a standardized multilingual grievance redressal framework, an independent Post Release Review Panel for OTT content, e-FIR implementation via I4C, amendments to the DSPE Act 1946 for CBI consent, and an Integrated Cybercrime Task Force.

The 260th Report on J&K and Ladakh reviews key development & security indicators: notes TFR decline to 1.5 and Multidimensional Poverty decline from 12.56% to 4.80%; highlights concerns over high FRA 2006 claim rejections (39,898 out of 46,242 claims) and high secondary school dropout rates (12.60%); recommends GI tag branding, fast-tracking lithium and mineral exploration, and climate-resilient infrastructure.

title: PRESS RELEASE ON THE 166th REPORT OF DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES, LAW AND JUSTICE
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:

upsc_summary: The Parliamentary Standing Committee's 166th Report evaluates the tribunal ecosystem across ITAT, RCT, TDSAT, NGT, and NCLT, calling for systemic structural reforms.
Recommends creating dedicated IBC Benches/verticals within NCLT to address severe pendency where 95% of staff is contractual and IBC statutory resolution timelines are routinely breached.

upsc_summary: The 175th Report on Vector-Borne Diseases in NE India advocates a region-specific Integrated Vector Management (IVM) strategy, expanding Viral Research & Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL), cross-border surveillance with Myanmar/Bangladesh, and creating a VBD funding window under NESIDS.

The 176th Report on Healthcare Affordability cites NSO 80th Round data showing private hospitalization (avg ₹50,508) is nearly 8x public cost (₹6,631); recommends capping essential private treatment costs, expanding Government Health Expenditure to 2.5% GDP target, establishing a voluntary insurance model for the 'missing middle' (30% population), and extending AB-PMJAY to all children under 5 and seniors over 60.

The 177th Report on Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) recommends establishing a National CKD Registry integrated with ABDM, mandating automatic eGFR reporting with every serum creatinine test, expanding home-based Peritoneal Dialysis under PMNDP, and extending AB-PMJAY post-transplant care coverage from 15 days to 1 year.

title: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: Legislative Reform: The MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was passed by Parliament, updating the 2006 Act to boost MSME competitiveness and ease of doing business.
Revised Classification & Free Registration: Standardizes MSME criteria across investment and turnover; makes registration voluntary and completely free on the national Udyam portal.

Mandatory TReDS Settlement: Mandates Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to settle MSME supplier invoices through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) platform to tackle delayed payments.

Dispute Resolution Framework: Permits States to set up multiple MSE Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs) and introduces strict statutory timelines: 90 days for mediation, referral to arbitration within 30 days upon failure, and 90 days for arbitral awards.

Legal Protection & Recovery: Requires courts to direct payment of at least 50% of the awarded amount to MSMEs during pending set-aside applications (>6 months); permits recovery of mediated settlements/awards as 'arrears of land revenue'.
Decriminalisation: Replaces criminal penal provisions for non-filing or minor non-disclosures with warnings and administrative fines.

The Alang-Sosiya cluster in Gujarat accounts for ~98% of India's ship recycling capacity, producing around 3.5 MMT of steel per annum without raw material exploitation.

Regulatory Framework: Governed by the Ship Recycling Act (2019), Ship Recycling Rules (2021), and Ship Recycling Regulations (2026), aligned with the Hong Kong International Convention (HKC) which entered into force globally on June 26, 2025.
Ship-breaking Credit Note Scheme (under SBFA 2.0): Grants credit notes worth 40% of recycled scrap value to incentivize domestic shipbuilding and compliant recycling.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 AUG 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: Amends the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 to introduce Section 9D, restricting State Governments from imposing fresh taxes or cesses on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands except under conditions set by the Central Government.
Declares uncollected or pending retrospective State levies on mineral rights invalid while preserving historical auction premiums and royalties that accrue directly to States.
Reaffirms that minor minerals (sand, gravel, granite, marble, etc.) remain entirely under the regulatory and fiscal jurisdiction of State Governments.
Aims to create a unified national mineral market, reduce cost escalation, protect critical and strategic mineral extraction, and curb high mineral imports (₹10.12 lakh crore in FY 2025-26).

Highlights structural reforms since 2014: State share in total mineral revenue rose to ~90% (₹1.14 lakh crore in 2025-26), supported by 723 major mineral block e-auctions, the National Critical Mineral Mission (₹16,300 crore), and 656 District Mineral Foundations (DMFs).

upsc_summary: Researchers from IASST Guwahati and IIT Guwahati have developed 'RK-251', a targeted smart cancer drug candidate designed to replace traditional chemotherapy.

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                19 AUG 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: MMDR Amendment Act, 2026 provides fiscal and tax predictability for mining projects to attract investment and cut import reliance on strategic/critical minerals.
Fiscal Federalism: Around 90% of overall mineral sector revenue (royalty, auction premium, DMF, GST share) accrues to State governments, maintaining state fiscal inflows.
National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM): Outlay of ₹16,300 crore up to FY 2030-31 to fund exploration, processing, and overseas asset acquisition (e.g., KABIL in Argentina).
Mining Reforms Framework: Mandates 100% competitive e-auctions since 2015, removal of captive mineral sale caps, and local welfare funding via District Mineral Foundations (DMF).
Regulatory Scope: Minor minerals (sand, gravel, granite) remain under the exclusive administrative and tax jurisdiction of State governments.

date:

upsc_summary: Overview: The Ken-Betwa Link Project (KBLP) is the flagship interlinking of rivers (ILR) project under the National Perspective Plan, costing ₹44,605 crore with a target completion date of 2030.

Key Infrastructure: Features the 96.7 m high Daudhan Dam on the Ken River in MP and a 216.47 km link canal to transfer surplus water from the Ken basin to the Betwa basin in UP, alongside Lower Orr, Kotha Barrage, and Bina Complex.

Developmental Benefits: Aims to provide year-round irrigation to 10.62 lakh hectares, drinking water to 62 lakh people across 14 water-starved districts of the Bundelkhand region (MP & UP), and generate 103 MW hydro plus 27 MW solar power.

Ecological & Social Safeguards: Incorporates an Integrated Landscape Management Plan (ILMP) for the Greater Panna Landscape under the Greater Panna Landscape Council (GPLC) for wildlife conservation (tigers, vultures, gharials); land acquisition and R&R follow the LARR Act 2013 and MP Special Package.

title: National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 AUG 2026 10:24AM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP): Launched in 2019 under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying to control and eradicate Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) and Brucellosis through nationwide mass vaccination.

Vaccination Strategy: Targets 100% biannual vaccination against FMD for all eligible livestock (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, pig) and a one-time lifetime Brucellosis vaccination for 4–8 month old female bovine calves.
Subsumation under LHDCP: NADCP, LH&DC, and Pashu Aushadhi are integrated under the umbrella Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) with a budget outlay of ₹2,010 crore for FY 2026–27.

Impact & Disease Reduction: FMD outbreaks declined from 132 (2019) to 40 (2025); Brucellosis outbreaks dropped from 22 (2019) to 15 (2025). No FMD Serotype Asia-1 outbreak reported in the past three years.

Production Data: India's milk production increased by 69.4% from 146.31 million tonnes (2014-15) to 247.87 million tonnes (2024-25), with target average bovine productivity set at 3,000 kg/animal/year by 2030.

Digital Integration & Infrastructure: Over 39 crore livestock registered on the Bharat Pashudhan Portal using 12-digit Tag IDs; 4,019 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) operational across 29 States/UTs (toll-free number 1962).

One Health & Pandemic Preparedness: Aligned with National One Health Mission and supported by a US$ 25 million G20 Pandemic Fund Project. Key frameworks released include Standard Veterinary Treatment Guidelines (SVTG) and Crisis Management Plan (CMP) for Animal Diseases.

upsc_summary: Regenerative Agriculture is a holistic farming approach focused on restoring soil health, improving soil organic matter, enhancing biodiversity, and increasing climate resilience through minimal soil disturbance, cover cropping, mulching, and integrating livestock.

National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF, 2024): Provides an output-based incentive of ₹4,000 per acre/year for two years, establishes 10,000 Bio-input Resource Centres, and has formed 18,786 clusters covering 8.80 lakh hectares with 18.19 lakh enrolled farmers.
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY, 2015): Promotes organic farming with ₹31,500 per hectare assistance over three years, covering 16.90 lakh hectares since inception.

Per Drop More Crop (PDMC): Focuses on micro-irrigation (drip and sprinkler systems) with 55% financial assistance for small/marginal farmers and 45% for others; has covered 109 lakh hectares with ₹26,325 crore in central assistance.

Rainfed Area Development (RAD): Encourages Integrated Farming Systems (IFS) combining crops, livestock, fisheries, and agroforestry in 20-hectare clusters, offering ₹30,000 per family assistance; has covered 9.53 lakh hectares benefitting 15.73 lakh farmers.

Soil Health Card Scheme (2015): Evaluates soil health across 12 parameters every 2 years; over 25.89 crore soil health cards have been generated and 70,002 Krishi Sakhis trained to support dissemination.
